text: Rust allows only one mutable reference at a time so it can prove that nothing else is reading or writing that value while it is being changed. That exclusivity prevents data races and the related memory-safety bugs from aliased mutation, including iterator invalidation and use-after-free.
thought:
The borrow checker prevents two mutable references to the same value from coexisting. This blocks data races and use-after-free bugs.

This enforces the aliasing XOR mutability rule. Aliased mutation through multiple mutable references causes iterator invalidation and use-after-free when one reference reallocates while another still points to the old data.

The compiler cannot assume exclusive access when two mutable references exist. This enables undefined behavior from aliased mutation.
